questions.memo:

questions.prompt: Explain THREE problems that plastics cause for the environment.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): made from non-renewable oil; take hundreds of years to break down; litter on land; ocean pollution harming marine life; release toxic fumes when burnt

questions.prompt: Which of these metals is ferrous?
questions.explanation: Ferrous metals contain iron. Steel is mostly iron; copper, aluminium and brass contain no iron.

questions.prompt: Iron rusts when it is in contact with:
questions.explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and water. Remove either one and it stops.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical name for rust?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

questions.prompt: Aluminium window frames rust if they are not painted.
questions.explanation: Aluminium is non-ferrous, so it cannot rust. It forms a thin protective oxide layer.

questions.prompt: Which metal is used to galvanise steel?
questions.explanation: Galvanising coats steel with zinc, which protects it even when scratched.

questions.prompt: Match each product with the most suitable preservation method.
Match each heat treatment with what it does.

pairs.right: Heat, then cool quickly; becomes hard but brittle

questions.prompt: Why do steel gates near the sea rust faster than those inland?
options: The sun is stronger at the coast
Salt in the moist air speeds up rusting
There is less oxygen at the coast

questions.prompt: Explain why a scratch in the paint on a steel car is a problem, but a scratch on a galvanised bucket is not.
questions.memo:
✓ paint only works as a barrier (1)
✓ a scratch lets water and oxygen reach the steel, so it rusts and the rust spreads under the paint (1)
✓ on galvanised steel the zinc corrodes instead of the steel / sacrificial protection (1)
✓ so the exposed steel is still protected (1)
